bull.b: Q2 revenue growth and reaffirmed FY2026 guidance indicate expanding commercial activity and a substantial demand base. If delivery execution holds, the higher sales trajectory can improve operating leverage, strengthen customer confidence, and support progress toward sustainable scale.

Bookings near $60M per quarter and 80% of second-half revenue covered provide visibility beyond a single project award. This contracted demand can support production planning, reduce order-timing uncertainty, and give FTC Solar a foundation to convert growth into recurring volume.

Approval by nine of the top ten EPCs, plus additions across large EPCs and developers, broadens access to influential buyers. A wider approved-vendor footprint can improve bid participation, diversify customer opportunities, and increase the ability to capture utility-scale projects over time.

bear.b: Despite top-line stabilization, TTM gross margin is only about 3.5% while EBIT and net margins remain deeply negative. This weak earnings base leaves little buffer against pricing or execution pressure and means revenue growth has not yet translated into durable profitability or internally funded expansion.

Repeated covenant waivers and the revised agreement show that liquidity remains a material operating constraint. Deferring repayment and suspending tests provide time, but future cash, revenue, EBITDA, and margin requirements could restrict flexibility if profitability does not improve.

Negative operating cash flow of $27.1M and negative free cash flow of $28.6M indicate the business is consuming cash while losses persist. Continued cash burn can force reliance on external capital or balance-sheet resources, limiting investment capacity and increasing execution risk.
